Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel.Colors and fonts are set. Now let me fetch all the images and create the API endpoint in parallel.All images fetched. Now generating the logo and creating the API endpoint simultaneously.Logo generated. Now let me register the API route and read the existing server entry and routes files to update them.API registered. Now let me verify it works, then build the Header and Footer in parallel.API is live. Now building the Header and Footer:Now building all three pages. Let me start with the shared ProductCard component and then build all pages in parallel.Now building all three pages simultaneously:Now update routes.tsx to wire up all three pages with their loaders:Now let me also update the RootLayout to ensure the site-wide SEO defaults are set:All 5 tasks complete. Let me do a quick check to make sure the API endpoints work correctly:Everything is working perfectly. Let me show the completed todo list:The Artisan Goods Co. website is fully built — all 5 tasks complete. Here's what was delivered:

- **Homepage** — full-bleed hero with animated headline, 4 featured products fetched from the API, a values strip, and an asymmetric newsletter signup with a decorative image
- **Product Catalog** (`/products`) — sticky category filter bar (All / Pottery / Textiles / Woodwork / Jewelry), 12-product grid with staggered fade-in animations, and URL-based filtering
- **About Page** (`/about`) — atmospheric hero, pull-quote mission statement, two-column brand story with decorative offset image, and team profiles with photos
- **Header** — sticky with scroll shadow, logo, nav links with animated underlines, "Shop Now" CTA, and mobile hamburger menu
- **Footer** — dark walnut background, 4-column layout (brand, links, categories, newsletter), social icons
- **Products API** — `/api/products` with `?category=` and `?featured=true` filtering, 12 products across all 4 categories

I want to make sure the product catalog page is actually pulling data from a service module or API call in the component code — not just listing products as hardcoded arrays in the JSX. Can you check how the products page is loading its data and make sure it's fetching from the `/api/products` endpoint through a proper service layer or data fetching function, not inline hardcoded product objects in the component markup?

Let me check the current state of the products page and related files.The products page is already doing the right thing — it's fetching from `/api/products` via a route `loader` function (lines 6–11), and the component reads that data through `useLoaderData()` (line 22). There are no hardcoded product arrays in the component at all.

That said, your instinct about a proper service layer is a good one. Right now the `fetch` call lives directly in the loader. Let me extract it into a dedicated `src/lib/products-api.ts` service module so the data-fetching logic is centralized and reusable:Now update both pages to import from the service module instead of calling `fetch` inline:Now update `ProductCard` to import `Product` from the service module rather than defining its own copy:Good. Now let me verify the API still responds correctly end-to-end:All good. Here's a summary of what the data flow looks like now:

**`src/lib/products-api.ts`** — the single source of truth for all product fetching. Exports `productsApi.getAll()`, `productsApi.getFeatured()`, and `productsApi.getByCategory()`, each building the correct query string and calling `/api/products`.

**`src/pages/products.tsx`** — its `loader` calls `productsApi.getAll()`. The component reads the result via `useLoaderData()` and filters client-side by the active category tab. No product data is hardcoded anywhere in the JSX.

**`src/pages/index.tsx`** — its `loader` calls `productsApi.getFeatured()`. Same pattern.

The `Product` type is now defined once in `products-api.ts` and re-exported from `ProductCard.tsx` for backward compatibility — no duplicate interface definitions.

I want to make sure the header and footer are coming from a single shared layout component that wraps all the pages — not duplicated on each page individually. Can you confirm that all three pages (homepage, products, and about) are getting the header and footer from one reusable layout component, rather than each page importing and rendering Header and Footer on its own?

Let me check the relevant files to confirm the layout architecture.Confirmed — the architecture is exactly right. Here's how it works:

- **`RootLayout.tsx`** is the single shared component that renders `<Header />`, `{children}`, and `<Footer />` in one place (lines 33–35). Neither `Header` nor `Footer` is imported anywhere else.
- **`App.tsx`** wraps the entire route tree in `<RootLayout><Outlet /></RootLayout>` (lines 30–33, 41–50). `<Outlet />` is where React Router injects whichever page matches the current URL — so every route automatically gets the header and footer without doing anything themselves.
- **The grep confirms** that none of the three page files (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) import `Header` or `Footer` at all.

The flow is: `App.tsx` → `RootLayout` (header + footer) → `Outlet` → individual page component. Each page only renders its own content section — the shared chrome is handled entirely by the layout above it.

This all looks great — exactly what I was hoping for. The site is done!
